data.title: Ransom Note
data.description: Given two strings ransomNote and magazine, return true if ransomNote can be constructed using the letters from magazine (each letter used at most as many times as it appears).
data.problem_statement: Given two strings ransomNote and magazine, return true if ransomNote can be constructed using the letters from magazine (each letter used at most as many times as it appears).
hints: Count the frequency of available letters in the magazine string.
Use an integer array of size 26 or a hash map to store magazine character counts.
Iterate through the ransomNote: decrement the count for each character; if any count drops below 0, return false.

data.title: Decode String
data.description: Given an encoded string in the format k[encoded_string], decode it, where the encoded_string is repeated k times. Nested encodings are allowed.
data.problem_statement: Given an encoded string in the format k[encoded_string], decode it, where the encoded_string is repeated k times. Nested encodings are allowed.
hints: Use two stacks (or a stack of pairs): one for multiplier counts and one for string segments.
Iterate through the string: build multi-digit numbers and characters.
On `[`, push the current count and current string onto stacks; on `]`, pop count and previous string, and repeat current string.

data.title: Binary Search
data.description: Given a sorted array of integers and a target, return the index of target if found, else -1, in O(log n) time.
data.problem_statement: Given a sorted array of integers and a target, return the index of target if found, else -1, in O(log n) time.
data.constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 10^4
nums is sorted ascending, all unique
hints: Binary search operates on a sorted array by dividing the search interval in half at each step.
Calculate `mid = left + Math.floor((right - left) / 2)` to avoid integer overflow.
If nums[mid] == target return mid; if nums[mid] < target search right (left = mid + 1); otherwise search left (right = mid - 1).

data.title: Koko Eating Bananas
data.description: Given piles of bananas and h hours, find the minimum eating speed k (bananas/hour) so Koko can finish all piles within h hours.
data.problem_statement: Given piles of bananas and h hours, find the minimum eating speed k (bananas/hour) so Koko can finish all piles within h hours.
hints: Binary search on the answer space: Koko's hourly eating speed k ranges from 1 to max(piles).
For a candidate speed k, total hours required = sum of `Math.ceil(pile / k)` across all piles.
If total hours <= h, k is valid, so search for a slower speed (right = mid); otherwise search for a faster speed (left = mid + 1).

data.title: Find Peak Element
data.description: Given an integer array, find a peak element (strictly greater than its neighbors) and return its index, in O(log n) time. Assume nums[-1] and nums[n] are -infinity.
data.problem_statement: Given an integer array, find a peak element (strictly greater than its neighbors) and return its index, in O(log n) time. Assume nums[-1] and nums[n] are -infinity.
data.constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 1000
Adjacent elements are never equal
hints: Compare nums[mid] with its neighbor nums[mid + 1] to determine the slope.
If nums[mid] < nums[mid + 1], an ascending slope exists, meaning a peak must exist to the right (left = mid + 1).
Otherwise, a descending slope exists, so a peak is at mid or to the left (right = mid).

data.title: Time Based Key-Value Store
data.description: Design a time-based key-value store: set(key, value, timestamp) stores the value, and get(key, timestamp) returns the value set at the largest timestamp <= given timestamp.
data.problem_statement: Design a time-based key-value store: set(key, value, timestamp) stores the value, and get(key, timestamp) returns the value set at the largest timestamp <= given timestamp.
hints: Use a hash map mapping each key to a sorted list of `(timestamp, value)` pairs.
Because timestamps are strictly increasing on `set`, the list for each key is sorted by timestamp.
On `get(key, timestamp)`, use binary search on the timestamp list to find the largest timestamp <= query timestamp.

data.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
data.description: Given two sorted arrays, return the median of the combined sorted array, in O(log(m+n)) time.
data.problem_statement: Given two sorted arrays, return the median of the combined sorted array, in O(log(m+n)) time.
hints: Binary search on the partition point of the smaller array to achieve O(log(min(m, n))) time.
Partition both arrays such that left halves contain (m + n + 1) / 2 elements.
Check if max(leftA, leftB) <= min(rightA, rightB) to calculate median from the boundary elements.

data.title: Rotate Array
data.description: Given an array, rotate it to the right by k steps, in-place, using O(1) extra space.
data.problem_statement: Given an array, rotate it to the right by k steps, in-place, using O(1) extra space.
hints: Rotating an array by k steps can be solved by reversing specific segments in-place.
First reverse the entire array of length n.
Then reverse the first k % n elements, and finally reverse the remaining n - (k % n) elements.

data.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
data.description: Given a string and an integer k, find the length of the longest substring achievable by replacing at most k characters with any character, such that all characters become the same.
data.problem_statement: Given a string and an integer k, find the length of the longest substring achievable by replacing at most k characters with any character, such that all characters become the same.
hints: To maximize window length with at most k replacements, focus on the count of the most frequent character in the window.
Maintain a frequency table and track the max frequency seen in any window.
If the number of other characters to replace (window_length - max_frequency) exceeds k, shrink the window from the left.

data.title: Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days
data.description: Given package weights and D days, find the minimum ship capacity so all packages can be shipped within D days, keeping weight order and daily loading capacity fixed.
data.problem_statement: Given package weights and D days, find the minimum ship capacity so all packages can be shipped within D days, keeping weight order and daily loading capacity fixed.
hints: Binary search on the conveyor ship capacity: min capacity is max(weights), max capacity is sum(weights).
For candidate capacity C, greedily load packages onto ships day by day to count required days.
If days <= D, capacity C is feasible, try smaller capacity (right = mid); otherwise increase capacity (left = mid + 1).

data.title: Search Insert Position
data.description: Given a sorted array and a target, return the index if found, or the index where it would be inserted in order, in O(log n) time.
data.problem_statement: Given a sorted array and a target, return the index if found, or the index where it would be inserted in order, in O(log n) time.
hints: Perform standard binary search to find target in the sorted array.
If nums[mid] == target, return index mid.
When the binary search loop terminates without finding target, the `left` pointer points precisely to the correct insertion index.

data.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
data.description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its node values (grouped by level, left to right).
data.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its node values (grouped by level, left to right).
hints: Level order traversal processes nodes layer by layer using Breadth-First Search (BFS).
Use a queue initialized with the root node.
At each level, record `levelSize = queue.length`, dequeue that many nodes into a level array, and enqueue their children.

data.title: Valid Parentheses
data.description: Given a string containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid — every open bracket must be closed by the same type in the correct order.
data.problem_statement: Given a string containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid — every open bracket must be closed by the same type in the correct order.
hints: A stack is the standard data structure for matching nested opening and closing delimiters.
When you see an opening bracket, push its corresponding closing bracket onto the stack.
When you see a closing bracket, check if the stack is non-empty and top matches; otherwise return false.

data.title: Diameter of Binary Tree
data.description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the length of the tree's diameter. The diameter is the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes.
data.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return the length of the tree's diameter. The diameter is the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes.
hints: The diameter is the length of the longest path between any two nodes in a tree.
For any node, the longest path passing through it as root is `left_height + right_height`.
Compute node height recursively while maintaining a global max diameter variable updated at each node.

data.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
data.description: Given the root of a binary search tree and two distinct node values p and q that exist in the tree, return the value of their lowest common ancestor.
data.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary search tree and two distinct node values p and q that exist in the tree, return the value of their lowest common ancestor.
data.constraints:
2 <= number of nodes <= 10^4
All node values are unique
p and q are guaranteed to exist in the tree
hints: Take advantage of the Binary Search Tree (BST) ordering property: left < root < right.
If both p and q values are strictly less than root.val, LCA lies in the left subtree.
If both are strictly greater than root.val, LCA lies in the right subtree; otherwise root is the split point and LCA.

data.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
data.description: Given the root of a binary tree, determine whether it satisfies the binary search tree property: every value in a left subtree is smaller than its node, and every value in a right subtree is larger.
data.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, determine whether it satisfies the binary search tree property: every value in a left subtree is smaller than its node, and every value in a right subtree is larger.
hints: Every node in a valid BST must satisfy `min_bound < node.val < max_bound`.
Pass down exclusive range boundaries `(min, max)` during depth-first traversal.
When recursing left update max = node.val; when recursing right update min = node.val; verify node value is within bounds.

data.title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
data.description: Given the preorder and inorder traversals of a binary tree with unique values, construct and return the original binary tree.
data.problem_statement: Given the preorder and inorder traversals of a binary tree with unique values, construct and return the original binary tree.
data.constraints:
1 <= preorder.length <= 3000
preorder.length == inorder.length
All values are unique
hints: The first value in preorder traversal is always the root of the tree.
Find root.val in inorder traversal: elements to its left form the left subtree, elements to its right form the right subtree.
Use a hash map for O(1) inorder index lookups and recursively construct left and right subtrees.

data.title: Two Sum II (Sorted Input)
data.description: Given a 1-indexed sorted array of integers, find two numbers that add up to a target and return their indices.
data.problem_statement: Given a 1-indexed sorted array of integers, find two numbers that add up to a target and return their indices.
hints: Because the array is already sorted, smaller sums are on the left and larger sums on the right.
Initialize two pointers at the two ends: left = 0 and right = n - 1.
If sum < target increment left; if sum > target decrement right; if sum == target return the 1-based indices.

data.title: Isomorphic Strings
data.description: Given two strings, determine if they are isomorphic — characters in one can be consistently replaced to get the other, with no two characters mapping to the same character.
data.problem_statement: Given two strings, determine if they are isomorphic — characters in one can be consistently replaced to get the other, with no two characters mapping to the same character.
hints: Two strings are isomorphic if there is a bijective (one-to-one and onto) mapping between their characters.
Maintain two hash maps or arrays tracking s -> t and t -> s character mappings.
For every index, verify both mappings match consistently; return false on any conflict.

data.title: Binary Tree Right Side View
data.description: Given the root of a binary tree, imagine viewing it from the right side and return the value of the node visible at each depth from top to bottom.
data.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, imagine viewing it from the right side and return the value of the node visible at each depth from top to bottom.
hints: The right side view consists of the rightmost node at each depth level.
Use BFS level-order traversal with a queue.
At each level, append the value of the last node in the queue to the output list.

data.title: Climbing Stairs
data.description: You are climbing a staircase with n steps. Each move can climb either 1 or 2 steps. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top.
data.problem_statement: You are climbing a staircase with n steps. Each move can climb either 1 or 2 steps. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top.
hints: To reach step n, you can either take 1 step from step n - 1 or 2 steps from step n - 2.
The recurrence relation is `dp[n] = dp[n - 1] + dp[n - 2]`, mirroring Fibonacci numbers.
Optimize space to O(1) by maintaining only the previous two step values.

data.title: House Robber
data.description: Given an array of money amounts in houses along a street, return the maximum amount you can rob without robbing two adjacent houses.
data.problem_statement: Given an array of money amounts in houses along a street, return the maximum amount you can rob without robbing two adjacent houses.
hints: At house i, choose between robbing it (nums[i] + max profit from house i - 2) or skipping it (max profit from house i - 1).
Recurrence: `dp[i] = max(dp[i - 1], dp[i - 2] + nums[i])`.
Maintain only two variables (prev1 and prev2) for O(1) auxiliary space.

data.title: Valid Anagram
data.description: Given two strings `s` and `t`, return true if `t` is an anagram of `s`.
data.problem_statement: Given two strings `s` and `t`, return true if `t` is an anagram of `s`.
data.constraints:
1 <= s.length, t.length <= 5*10^4
Lowercase English letters only
hints: Two strings are anagrams if and only if they have identical character counts.
Use a frequency array of size 26 or a hash map to count character frequencies.
Increment counts for characters in s and decrement for t; all counts must end at zero.

data.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
data.description: Given an integer array, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
data.problem_statement: Given an integer array, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
hints: Let `dp[i]` be the length of the longest increasing subsequence ending at index i.
Initialize all `dp[i] = 1`. For every earlier j < i where nums[j] < nums[i], update `dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + 1)`.
For O(n log n) time complexity, maintain an array of smallest tail values using binary search (patience sorting).

data.title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
data.description: Given a positive integer array, determine whether it can be split into two subsets with equal sums.
data.problem_statement: Given a positive integer array, determine whether it can be split into two subsets with equal sums.
hints: Partitioning into two equal subsets requires finding a subset that sums to `total_sum / 2`.
If total_sum is odd, return false immediately.
Use 0/1 Knapsack DP: let `dp[s]` be boolean whether subset sum s is achievable; iterate backwards to ensure each element is used at most once.

data.title: Decode Ways
data.description: A message containing digits can be decoded using 1-26 mapped to A-Z. Return the number of ways to decode the string. A zero cannot be decoded alone.
data.problem_statement: A message containing digits can be decoded using 1-26 mapped to A-Z. Return the number of ways to decode the string. A zero cannot be decoded alone.
hints: Let `dp[i]` be the number of ways to decode substring s[0..i].
A single digit s[i] is valid if s[i] != '0' (contributes dp[i - 1]).
Two digits s[i-1..i] are valid if "10" <= s[i-1..i] <= "26" (contributes dp[i - 2]).

data.title: Palindromic Substrings
data.description: Given a string, return the number of palindromic substrings it contains (counting different positions with the same substring as separate).
data.problem_statement: Given a string, return the number of palindromic substrings it contains (counting different positions with the same substring as separate).
hints: Every single character and every identical adjacent pair can serve as the center of palindromes.
Expand outwards from each of the 2n - 1 potential centers.
Count 1 for every valid expansion step where left and right characters match.

data.title: Contains Duplicate
data.description: Given an integer array, return true if any value appears at least twice.
data.problem_statement: Given an integer array, return true if any value appears at least twice.
hints: Consider what data structure provides O(1) average lookup time for previously seen values.
A Hash Set allows checking whether an element has already appeared in the array.
Iterate through the array; if the current number is already present in the set return true, else add it.

data.title: Implement Queue using Stacks
data.description: Implement a FIFO queue using only two stacks, supporting push, pop, peek, and empty operations.
data.problem_statement: Implement a FIFO queue using only two stacks, supporting push, pop, peek, and empty operations.
hints: You can implement a FIFO Queue using two LIFO Stacks: `in_stack` for enqueue and `out_stack` for dequeue.
Push operations always push onto `in_stack`.
For pop/peek: if `out_stack` is empty, transfer all elements from `in_stack` to `out_stack` (reversing their order), then pop from `out_stack`.

data.title: Design HashMap
data.description: Design a HashMap without using any built-in hash table library, supporting put(key, value), get(key), and remove(key) operations.
data.problem_statement: Design a HashMap without using any built-in hash table library, supporting put(key, value), get(key), and remove(key) operations.
data.constraints:
0 <= key, value <= 10^6
At most 10^4 calls total
data.example_input: put(1,1); put(2,2); get(1); get(3); put(2,1); get(2); remove(2); get(2)
hints: Design a hash map using an array of buckets and separate chaining (linked list or list of pairs) to handle collisions.
Choose a large prime number (e.g. 10007) for the bucket array size to distribute keys evenly.
Implement `put`, `get`, and `remove` by hashing the key to a bucket index and scanning the bucket.

data.title: Valid Palindrome II
data.description: Given a string, return true if it can become a palindrome after deleting at most one character.
data.problem_statement: Given a string, return true if it can become a palindrome after deleting at most one character.
hints: Start two pointers from the left and right ends of the string and move inward while characters match.
On the first mismatch between s[left] and s[right], you are allowed to delete at most one character.
Check whether the remaining substring s[left + 1..right] or s[left..right - 1] is a palindrome.

data.title: Sort Colors
data.description: Given an array with only values 0, 1, and 2, sort it in-place in a single pass without using a library sort.
data.problem_statement: Given an array with only values 0, 1, and 2, sort it in-place in a single pass without using a library sort.
hints: Use the Dutch National Flag 3-way partitioning algorithm with three pointers: low, mid, and high.
All elements before low are 0, between low and mid are 1, and after high are 2.
If nums[mid] is 0 swap with low and increment both; if 1 increment mid; if 2 swap with high and decrement high.

data.title: Set Matrix Zeroes
data.description: Given an m x n matrix, if an element is 0, set its entire row and column to 0, in-place, using O(1) extra space.
data.problem_statement: Given an m x n matrix, if an element is 0, set its entire row and column to 0, in-place, using O(1) extra space.
hints: To achieve O(1) extra space, use the first row and first column of the matrix as marker arrays.
Use two boolean flags to record whether the first row and first column originally contained zeros.
Iterate through the rest of the matrix marking matrix[i][0] and matrix[0][j] with 0, then update cells based on markers.

data.title: Top K Frequent Elements
data.description: Given an integer array and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements, in any order.
data.problem_statement: Given an integer array and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements, in any order.
data.constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
k is guaranteed to be valid
hints: First compute the frequency of each unique number using a hash map.
To find the top k frequent elements, you can use bucket sort where bucket index represents frequency.
Traverse the buckets from highest frequency (n) down to 1 and collect elements until k items are collected in O(n) time.

data.title: Search a 2D Matrix
data.description: Given an m x n matrix where each row is sorted and the first element of each row is greater than the last of the previous row, determine if a target value exists, in O(log(m*n)) time.
data.problem_statement: Given an m x n matrix where each row is sorted and the first element of each row is greater than the last of the previous row, determine if a target value exists, in O(log(m*n)) time.
hints: Treat the m x n 2D matrix as a virtual 1D sorted array of length m * n.
Map a 1D index `mid` to 2D matrix coordinates: `row = Math.floor(mid / n)` and `col = mid % n`.
Perform standard binary search between left = 0 and right = m * n - 1.

data.title: Group Anagrams
data.description: Given an array of strings, group the anagrams together and return the groups in any order.
data.problem_statement: Given an array of strings, group the anagrams together and return the groups in any order.
hints: Anagrams have the same character frequency signature or sorted string representation.
Use the sorted version of each word or a tuple of character frequencies as the hash map key.
Group all original words with the same key together in the hash map values.

data.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
data.description: Given a string, return the longest palindromic substring within it.
data.problem_statement: Given a string, return the longest palindromic substring within it.
hints: Every palindrome is symmetric around its center.
There are 2n - 1 potential centers (n single characters and n - 1 adjacent character pairs).
Expand outwards from each center while characters match and track the longest palindromic substring.

data.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
data.description: Evaluate the value of an arithmetic expression given in Reverse Polish Notation (postfix), where operands and operators are separated tokens.
data.problem_statement: Evaluate the value of an arithmetic expression given in Reverse Polish Notation (postfix), where operands and operators are separated tokens.
hints: Reverse Polish Notation (postfix) places operators after their operands.
Iterate through the tokens: when a number is seen, push it onto the stack.
When an operator (+, -, *, /) is seen, pop the top two operands, apply the operation (note operand order for - and /), and push the result.

data.title: Maximum Product Subarray
data.description: Given an integer array `nums`, find the contiguous subarray with the largest product and return that product.
data.problem_statement: Given an integer array `nums`, find the contiguous subarray with the largest product and return that product.
hints: Multiplying by a negative number flips the sign: a minimum negative product can become a maximum positive product.
Maintain both current maximum and current minimum products at each position.
When the current number is negative, swap the current max and min before multiplying.

data.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
data.description: Given a rotated sorted array of unique integers and a target, return the index of target, or -1 if not present, in O(log n) time.
data.problem_statement: Given a rotated sorted array of unique integers and a target, return the index of target, or -1 if not present, in O(log n) time.
hints: In a rotated sorted array without duplicates, one half of the array across mid is always strictly sorted.
Identify whether the left half nums[left..mid] or the right half is sorted.
Check if the target lies within the boundaries of the sorted half to decide which subarray to search.

data.title: Two Sum
data.description: Given an array of integers `nums` and a target value, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to the target. Assume exactly one valid answer exists, and the same element cannot be used twice.
data.problem_statement: Given an array of integers `nums` and a target value, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to the target. Assume exactly one valid answer exists, and the same element cannot be used twice.
data.constraints:
2 <= nums.length <= 10^4
-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
Exactly one valid answer exists
hints: Think about what information you need to remember while scanning the array.
For each number, consider whether its complement (target - nums[i]) has already been seen.
A hash map allows fast O(1) lookup of previously seen values and their indices.

data.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
data.description: Given an array of daily stock prices, find the maximum profit achievable by buying on one day and selling on a later day. Return 0 if no profit is possible.
data.problem_statement: Given an array of daily stock prices, find the maximum profit achievable by buying on one day and selling on a later day. Return 0 if no profit is possible.
hints: To maximize profit, you want to buy at the lowest price before you sell.
Keep track of the minimum stock price encountered so far as you iterate from left to right.
At each day, calculate the potential profit by subtracting min_price from current price, and update the global max profit.

data.title: Product of Array Except Self
data.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return an array where each element is the product of all elements except itself, without using division, in O(n) time.
data.problem_statement: Given an integer array `nums`, return an array where each element is the product of all elements except itself, without using division, in O(n) time.
hints: The product of all elements except nums[i] equals (product of all elements to the left of i) * (product of all elements to the right of i).
Calculate the prefix products in a first pass from left to right.
In a second pass from right to left, maintain a running suffix product and multiply with the prefix product.

data.title: 3Sum
data.description: Given an integer array, return all unique triplets that sum to zero.
data.problem_statement: Given an integer array, return all unique triplets that sum to zero.
hints: Sorting the array reduces this problem to Two Sum II with Two Pointers.
Iterate through the array fixing nums[i] as the first element; skip duplicate values of nums[i].
For the remaining subarray, use two pointers (left and right) to find pairs that sum to -nums[i].

data.title: 3Sum Closest
data.description: Given an integer array and a target, find three integers whose sum is closest to the target and return that sum.
data.problem_statement: Given an integer array and a target, find three integers whose sum is closest to the target and return that sum.
hints: Sort the array first to enable two-pointer scanning for each fixed element.
Iterate through the array fixing nums[i], then use left = i + 1 and right = n - 1.
At each step, calculate the sum, update the closest sum if |target - sum| is smaller, and adjust left or right accordingly.

data.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
data.description: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth (number of nodes along the longest path from root to a leaf).
data.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth (number of nodes along the longest path from root to a leaf).
hints: The maximum depth of a binary tree is 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)).
Base case: if the current node is null, its depth is 0.
Recursively compute the maximum depth of left and right subtrees and return 1 + Math.max(leftDepth, rightDepth).

data.title: Trapping Rain Water
data.description: Given an array representing elevation map bar heights, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
data.problem_statement: Given an array representing elevation map bar heights, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
hints: The water trapped above bar i depends on min(left_max, right_max) - height[i].
Use two pointers starting at left = 0 and right = n - 1 with running left_max and right_max.
Process the side with the smaller max height and move that pointer inward while accumulating trapped water.

data.title: Min Stack
data.description: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element, all in O(1) time.
data.problem_statement: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element, all in O(1) time.
data.example_input: push(-2); push(0); push(-3); getMin(); pop(); top(); getMin()
hints: A stack needs to support push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element in O(1) time.
Maintain a secondary stack (or store pairs in a single stack) to keep track of the minimum value at each depth.
When pushing x, push min(x, current_min) to the min-stack; pop from both stacks together.

data.title: Daily Temperatures
data.description: Given an array of daily temperatures, return an array where each element is the number of days until a warmer temperature; 0 if none exists.
data.problem_statement: Given an array of daily temperatures, return an array where each element is the number of days until a warmer temperature; 0 if none exists.
hints: To find the number of days until a warmer temperature, use a monotonic decreasing stack of indices.
Iterate through temperatures: while the current temperature is warmer than the temperature at the stack top index, pop and calculate the day difference.
Push the current day index onto the stack.

data.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
data.description: Given a string, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
data.problem_statement: Given a string, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
hints: Use a dynamic sliding window where all characters in the window are unique.
Maintain a hash map recording the most recent index of each character.
When a repeated character is encountered, jump the left boundary to max(left, last_seen_index + 1).

data.title: Car Fleet
data.description: Given positions and speeds of cars heading to the same destination, return the number of car fleets that will arrive (cars that catch up to a slower car ahead merge into one fleet).
data.problem_statement: Given positions and speeds of cars heading to the same destination, return the number of car fleets that will arrive (cars that catch up to a slower car ahead merge into one fleet).
hints: Sort the cars in descending order by their starting positions so you process cars from closest to target to farthest.
Calculate the time each car needs to reach the target: (target - position) / speed.
If a car behind takes less or equal time than the car ahead, it will catch up and join that fleet; otherwise it forms a new fleet.

data.title: Path Sum
data.description: Given the root of a binary tree and a target sum, determine whether there is a root-to-leaf path whose node values add up exactly to the target sum.
data.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree and a target sum, determine whether there is a root-to-leaf path whose node values add up exactly to the target sum.
hints: Traverse from root to leaf using DFS, subtracting node values from targetSum.
Base case: if current node is a leaf (no left and no right child), check if `node.val == current_target`.
Recursively check if `hasPathSum(node.left, target - node.val) || hasPathSum(node.right, target - node.val)`.

data.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
data.description: Given an integer array and an integer k, return the total number of contiguous subarrays whose sum equals k.
data.problem_statement: Given an integer array and an integer k, return the total number of contiguous subarrays whose sum equals k.
hints: The sum of any subarray nums[i..j] is equal to prefix_sum[j] - prefix_sum[i - 1].
We need prefix_sum[i - 1] = prefix_sum[j] - k to exist prior to index j.
Maintain a hash map storing the frequency of running prefix sums seen so far, initialized with `{0: 1}`.

data.title: Linked List Cycle
data.description: Given the head of a linked list, determine if the list has a cycle, using O(1) extra space.
data.problem_statement: Given the head of a linked list, determine if the list has a cycle, using O(1) extra space.
data.example_input: head = [3,2,0,-4], pos = 1 (tail connects to node index 1)
hints: Use Floyd's Cycle-Finding Algorithm (Fast and Slow pointers).
Initialize slow pointer moving 1 step at a time and fast pointer moving 2 steps at a time.
If fast reaches null, there is no cycle; if fast and slow meet at the same node, a cycle exists.

data.title: Middle of the Linked List
data.description: Given the head of a singly linked list, return the middle node. If there are two middle nodes, return the second one.
data.problem_statement: Given the head of a singly linked list, return the middle node. If there are two middle nodes, return the second one.
hints: Use two pointers: a slow pointer moving 1 step and a fast pointer moving 2 steps.
Both pointers start at the head of the linked list.
When fast reaches the end (fast is null or fast.next is null), slow will be exactly at the middle node.

data.title: Same Tree
data.description: Given the roots of two binary trees, determine if they are structurally identical with the same node values.
data.problem_statement: Given the roots of two binary trees, determine if they are structurally identical with the same node values.
data.constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in each tree <= 100
hints: Two binary trees are structurally identical with same values if both roots match and their respective subtrees match.
Base cases: if both nodes are null return true; if one is null or values differ return false.
Recursively check `isSameTree(p.left, q.left) && isSameTree(p.right, q.right)`.

data.title: Coin Change
data.description: Given coin denominations and a target amount, return the fewest coins needed to make the amount. Return -1 if the amount cannot be formed.
data.problem_statement: Given coin denominations and a target amount, return the fewest coins needed to make the amount. Return -1 if the amount cannot be formed.
hints: Let `dp[a]` represent the minimum number of coins needed to make amount `a`.
Initialize `dp` array of size `amount + 1` with Infinity and set `dp[0] = 0`.
For each amount from 1 to target and for each coin: if coin <= amount, update `dp[amount] = min(dp[amount], 1 + dp[amount - coin])`.

data.title: Minimum Window Substring
data.description: Given strings `s` and `t`, find the minimum window substring of `s` that contains every character of `t` (including duplicates). Return empty string if none exists.
data.problem_statement: Given strings `s` and `t`, find the minimum window substring of `s` that contains every character of `t` (including duplicates). Return empty string if none exists.
hints: Use a sliding window with two pointers: expand the right pointer until all characters of t are included.
Maintain a count of required distinct character frequencies satisfied in the current window.
Once valid, contract the left pointer to minimize window length while maintaining all required character counts.

data.title: Encode and Decode Strings
data.description: Design an algorithm to encode a list of strings into one string, and decode it back to the original list of strings, handling strings that may contain any characters including delimiters.
data.problem_statement: Design an algorithm to encode a list of strings into one string, and decode it back to the original list of strings, handling strings that may contain any characters including delimiters.
hints: Use a delimiter-based length-prefix encoding format (e.g. `length#string`) to avoid ambiguity.
To encode: prefix each string with its length followed by a special delimiter like `#`.
To decode: read the integer length before `#`, extract that exact number of characters, and repeat.

data.title: Fruit Into Baskets
data.description: Given an array representing fruit types on trees, find the length of the longest subarray containing at most 2 distinct fruit types.
data.problem_statement: Given an array representing fruit types on trees, find the length of the longest subarray containing at most 2 distinct fruit types.
hints: This problem is equivalent to finding the longest contiguous subarray with at most 2 distinct elements.
Use a sliding window with a hash map tracking fruit types and their frequencies.
When the number of unique fruit types in the window exceeds 2, shrink the window from the left.

data.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
data.description: A sorted array has been rotated at an unknown pivot. Find the minimum element in O(log n) time.
data.problem_statement: A sorted array has been rotated at an unknown pivot. Find the minimum element in O(log n) time.
hints: In a rotated sorted array, binary search can compare the middle element with the rightmost element.
If nums[mid] > nums[right], the inflection point and minimum element must be strictly in the right half (left = mid + 1).
Otherwise, the minimum is at mid or in the left half (right = mid).

data.title: Valid Palindrome
data.description: Given a string, determine if it is a palindrome after converting to lowercase and removing non-alphanumeric characters.
data.problem_statement: Given a string, determine if it is a palindrome after converting to lowercase and removing non-alphanumeric characters.
data.example_input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"
hints: A valid palindrome reads identical backwards and forwards after removing non-alphanumeric characters.
Use two pointers starting at the beginning (left = 0) and end (right = n - 1) of the string.
Skip non-alphanumeric characters and compare lowercase versions; move pointers inward.

data.title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
data.description: Given an array of positive integers and a target sum, find the minimal length of a contiguous subarray whose sum is >= target. Return 0 if no such subarray exists.
data.problem_statement: Given an array of positive integers and a target sum, find the minimal length of a contiguous subarray whose sum is >= target. Return 0 if no such subarray exists.
hints: Since all numbers are positive, expanding the right window pointer monotonically increases the subarray sum.
Expand right pointer, adding nums[right] to current_sum.
While current_sum >= target, update the minimum length and shrink the window from the left by subtracting nums[left++].

data.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
data.description: Given an unsorted array of integers, return the length of the longest sequence of consecutive integers, in O(n) time.
data.problem_statement: Given an unsorted array of integers, return the length of the longest sequence of consecutive integers, in O(n) time.
hints: Insert all numbers into a Hash Set for O(1) lookup.
Only attempt to count a sequence starting from numbers where `num - 1` is not in the set.
For each sequence start, count consecutive numbers `num + 1`, `num + 2`... to achieve overall O(n) time.

data.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
data.description: Given the head of a linked list, remove the nth node from the end and return the head, in one pass.
data.problem_statement: Given the head of a linked list, remove the nth node from the end and return the head, in one pass.
data.constraints:
1 <= number of nodes <= 30
1 <= n <= number of nodes
hints: Use two pointers separated by a gap of n nodes.
Advance the first pointer n steps ahead of the second pointer.
Move both pointers forward together until the first pointer reaches the end; the second pointer will be right before the target node.

data.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
data.description: Given an array representing histogram bar heights (width 1 each), find the area of the largest rectangle in the histogram.
data.problem_statement: Given an array representing histogram bar heights (width 1 each), find the area of the largest rectangle in the histogram.
hints: Each bar can be the shortest bar of a rectangle bounded by the first smaller bar to its left and to its right.
Use a monotonic increasing stack storing bar indices.
When a smaller bar is encountered, pop bars and compute rectangle area using the popped bar height and width determined by stack indices.

data.title: Invert Binary Tree
data.description: Given the root of a binary tree, invert it (swap every left and right child) and return the new root.
data.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, invert it (swap every left and right child) and return the new root.
hints: To invert a tree, swap the left and right children of every node in the tree.
Base case: if root is null, return null.
Recursively invert the left and right subtrees, then swap `root.left` and `root.right`.

data.title: Container With Most Water
data.description: Given an array of heights representing vertical lines, find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container holding the most water.
data.problem_statement: Given an array of heights representing vertical lines, find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container holding the most water.
hints: The area is limited by the shorter of the two boundary lines multiplied by the distance between them.
Start with the maximum possible width using two pointers at both ends: left = 0, right = n - 1.
Always move the pointer pointing to the shorter vertical line inward to seek a taller line.

data.title: Merge Intervals
data.description: Given an array of intervals, merge all overlapping intervals and return the resulting non-overlapping set.
data.problem_statement: Given an array of intervals, merge all overlapping intervals and return the resulting non-overlapping set.
hints: Sorting intervals by their start times brings overlapping intervals next to each other.
Maintain a merged list of intervals initialized with the first interval.
If the current interval starts before the last merged interval ends, merge them by extending the end time to max(end1, end2).

data.title: Permutation in String
data.description: Given two strings s1 and s2, return true if s2 contains a permutation of s1 as a contiguous substring.
data.problem_statement: Given two strings s1 and s2, return true if s2 contains a permutation of s1 as a contiguous substring.
hints: A permutation of s1 in s2 means a substring of s2 with length equal to s1.length() having the exact same character frequencies.
Use a fixed-size sliding window of length s1.length() over s2.
Compare character frequency counts between s1 and the window; return true when they match.

data.title: Maximum Subarray
data.description: Given an integer array `nums`, find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum and return that sum.
data.problem_statement: Given an integer array `nums`, find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum and return that sum.
hints: A negative prefix will only reduce the sum of any subsequent subarray.
Maintain a running current_sum. If current_sum becomes negative, reset it to 0.
This is Kadane's algorithm: at each index, max_ending_here = max(num, max_ending_here + num).

data.title: Asteroid Collision
data.description: Given an array representing asteroids moving right (positive) or left (negative) with magnitude as size, simulate collisions (larger survives, equal both explode) and return the final state.
data.problem_statement: Given an array representing asteroids moving right (positive) or left (negative) with magnitude as size, simulate collisions (larger survives, equal both explode) and return the final state.
hints: Use a stack to simulate moving asteroids from left to right.
Positive asteroids move right (push to stack); negative asteroids move left and collide with positive asteroids on the stack top.
Handle collision: smaller explodes, equal size both explode, larger destroys the smaller asteroid.

data.title: Balanced Binary Tree
data.description: Given the root of a binary tree, determine whether the tree is height-balanced. A binary tree is height-balanced when the heights of the left and right subtrees of every node differ by at most 1.
data.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary tree, determine whether the tree is height-balanced. A binary tree is height-balanced when the heights of the left and right subtrees of every node differ by at most 1.
hints: A tree is height-balanced if for every node, the height difference between its left and right subtrees is at most 1.
Use post-order DFS to compute subtree heights from bottom to top in O(n) time.
Return -1 as a sentinel value immediately when any subtree is unbalanced to short-circuit the recursion.

data.title: Target Sum
data.description: Given a list of non-negative integers, assign either a plus or minus sign to every number so that the resulting expression equals target. Return the number of different sign assignments that achieve the target.
data.problem_statement: Given a list of non-negative integers, assign either a plus or minus sign to every number so that the resulting expression equals target. Return the number of different sign assignments that achieve the target.
hints: Let P be sum of positive numbers and N be sum of negative numbers: `P - N = target` and `P + N = total_sum`.
Adding equations gives `2P = target + total_sum => P = (target + total_sum) / 2`.
If target + total_sum is odd or target > total_sum, return 0; otherwise count subsets with sum P using standard 0/1 knapsack DP.

data.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
data.description: Given the root of a binary search tree and an integer k, return the value of the kth smallest node in the tree, where k is 1-indexed.
data.problem_statement: Given the root of a binary search tree and an integer k, return the value of the kth smallest node in the tree, where k is 1-indexed.
data.constraints:
1 <= number of nodes <= 10^4
1 <= k <= number of nodes
All node values are unique
hints: An in-order traversal (Left -> Root -> Right) of a BST visits node values in strictly ascending order.
Perform an iterative in-order traversal using an explicit stack.
Decrement k at each visited node; when k reaches 0, return the current node value.

data.title: Unique Paths
data.description: A robot starts at the top-left of an m x n grid and can move only right or down. Return the number of distinct paths to the bottom-right cell.
data.problem_statement: A robot starts at the top-left of an m x n grid and can move only right or down. Return the number of distinct paths to the bottom-right cell.
hints: To reach grid cell (r, c), a robot can only move from cell above (r - 1, c) or cell to the left (r, c - 1).
Recurrence: `dp[r][c] = dp[r - 1][c] + dp[r][c - 1]`.
Initialize the top row and left column to 1, and compute entries row by row.

data.title: Word Break
data.description: Given a string and a dictionary of words, determine whether the string can be segmented into a space-separated sequence of one or more dictionary words. A dictionary word may be reused.
data.problem_statement: Given a string and a dictionary of words, determine whether the string can be segmented into a space-separated sequence of one or more dictionary words. A dictionary word may be reused.
hints: Let `dp[i]` be true if prefix substring s[0..i] can be segmented into dictionary words.
Set `dp[0] = true` for the empty string.
For each i from 1 to s.length: check all j < i; if `dp[j]` is true and `wordDict` contains s[j..i], set `dp[i] = true`.

data.title: House Robber II
data.description: Houses are arranged in a circle, so the first and last houses are adjacent. Return the maximum amount of money that can be robbed without robbing adjacent houses.
data.problem_statement: Houses are arranged in a circle, so the first and last houses are adjacent. Return the maximum amount of money that can be robbed without robbing adjacent houses.
hints: Because houses are arranged in a circle, the first and last houses cannot both be robbed.
Decompose into two independent linear subproblems: `rob(nums[0..n-2])` and `rob(nums[1..n-1])`.
Return the maximum of the two results.

data.title: Minimum Path Sum
data.description: Given a grid of non-negative numbers, find a path from the top-left to the bottom-right that minimizes the sum of all visited cells. You may move only right or down.
data.problem_statement: Given a grid of non-negative numbers, find a path from the top-left to the bottom-right that minimizes the sum of all visited cells. You may move only right or down.
hints: To find the minimum path sum to cell (r, c), add grid[r][c] to the minimum of paths from above or from left.
Recurrence: `grid[r][c] += min(grid[r - 1][c], grid[r][c - 1])`.
Initialize the first row and column by cumulative sums and update grid in place.

data.title: Longest Common Subsequence
data.description: Given two strings, return the length of their longest subsequence that appears in both strings. A subsequence keeps character order but may skip characters.
data.problem_statement: Given two strings, return the length of their longest subsequence that appears in both strings. A subsequence keeps character order but may skip characters.
data.constraints:
1 <= text1.length, text2.length <= 1000
text1 and text2 contain lowercase English letters
hints: Let `dp[i][j]` be the length of Longest Common Subsequence between prefixes text1[0..i-1] and text2[0..j-1].
Otherwise, take the maximum from skipping a character: `dp[i][j] = max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1])`.
